result:
I don't have access to your dashboards, monitoring stack, or the incident channel, so I can't actually check the graph for you — I can only reason about what you've told me.

That said, the detail you mentioned in passing is the important one: EU checkout traffic moved to the new routing cluster last month, but this is "the same dashboard we've used all year." That's a real reason for doubt, not just a footnote. Two ways this bites you:

- **Query scope**: if the dashboard's data source/query was defined before the migration, it may not include the new cluster at all. A flat zero could mean "no errors" or it could mean "no data from EU" — those look identical on a line chart.
- **Silent traffic drop**: if EU checkout requests are quietly not being counted, you'd also expect total request volume to look artificially low, not just errors. Worth glancing at whether overall traffic on the dashboard matches expected volume (including EU), not just the error line.

Given the pricing-service config that got reverted was presumably global (not EU-specific), it's plausible EU was affected too and just isn't visible right now.

Before posting all-clear, I'd confirm with whoever owns the dashboard/migration that it's actually scoped to include the new EU cluster — or pull a quick EU-only error/volume check if one exists. That's a 5-minute check, not a blocker for the all-hands, but skipping it risks closing an incident that's still live for EU users. If you can't confirm in time, safer to post "reverted fix looks effective, confirming full coverage including EU cluster, will update shortly" rather than a flat all-clear.
